title: Matrix Similarity After Cyclic Shifts
summary: Given an m x n integer matrix and an integer k, perform k cycles of row shifts: even-indexed rows are shifted left, odd-indexed rows are shifted right.
statement: Given an m x n integer matrix and an integer k, perform k cycles of row shifts: even-indexed rows are shifted left, odd-indexed rows are shifted right. Return true if the final matrix matches the original, false otherwise.
constraints: Shift every even-indexed row left by k positions and every odd-indexed row right by k positions.
Rows wrap around and all have the same width.
Return whether the matrix is identical to its original state after all shifts.
hints: A row equals either its left or right k-shift exactly when it is periodic by k positions.
Reduce k modulo the row width.
For every row and column compare the value with the position shift steps away.
The equality condition checks every destination/source pair; direction is immaterial when testing invariance.
editorial: The equality condition checks every destination/source pair; direction is immaterial when testing invariance.

tests.explanation: A shift of four is one position modulo width three, and the rows change.
Both period-two and constant rows are unchanged by two positions.
